subject.title: [Feature Request] Telegram inline buttons for pairing approve/deny

question: Should Telegram callback buttons be allowed to approve or deny pairing/device requests, and what scopes must a button press prove for DM pairing versus operator.admin browser/device approval?
rationale: The requested UX moves trust-changing approval into Telegram callback handling, and current source intentionally separates command-owner pairing scope from operator.admin approval authority.

options.title: Define typed approval actions
options.body: Create reusable approval actions with request id, action, expiry, single-use handling, callback identity, durable-state checks, and existing scope enforcement before rendering Telegram buttons.

options.title: Limit to low-scope DM pairing
options.body: Add buttons only for sender DM pairing and leave operator.admin browser/device approvals on CLI or Control UI until a broader step-up model is approved.

options.title: Defer chat approval
options.body: Keep the command-copy workflow until channel-aware device approvals and chat-originated step-up authorization are settled.

recommendation.title: Define typed approval actions
recommendation.body: Create reusable approval actions with request id, action, expiry, single-use handling, callback identity, durable-state checks, and existing scope enforcement before rendering Telegram buttons.
